name: Machi
overview: Machi was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known primarily as the father of Geuel. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture does not provide further details about his life or character. His mention is brief and specific, focusing on his role within his family and tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Machi appears only once in Scripture and is a proper name. It is understood to possibly mean 'reduced' or 'bought,' though this meaning is not explicitly connected to his character or story. The name was not given directly by God but is recorded in Numbers 13:15.
familyAndRelationships: Machi is identified as the father of Geuel, establishing a direct paternal relationship. He is also noted as a descendant of the tribe of Gad. Scripture does not record any other family connections or relationships for Machi beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Machi's significance lies chiefly in his identification as the father of Geuel, who was one of the men sent to spy out the land of Canaan. This places Machi within the broader narrative of Israel's journey and God's unfolding plan for His people through the tribe of Gad. While Machi himself does not play an active role in the biblical account, his mention helps preserve the genealogical and tribal context crucial to understanding Israel's history.
